data.mechanism: A second feedback arm: inhibiting mTORC1 releases a PI3K-dependent brake and MAPK signalling goes up. Together with S6K1-IRS1 this is why single-agent mTOR inhibition tends to be met by compensatory growth signalling.
data.mechanism_beginner: Blocking mTORC1 can backfire by releasing a brake on a different growth pathway (MAPK) – one reason mTOR-blocking drugs alone often aren't enough.
data.context: The arrow records a feedback, not a direct action of active mTORC1 on ERK. What CAR2008 measured is that inhibiting mTORC1 raises MAPK signalling through a PI3K-dependent loop, and in patient tumours the rise depended on the dosing schedule.
data.boundary: Single-study edge in this corpus, which says nothing about how replicated the loop is in the wider literature. CAR2008 includes tumour biopsies from patients with advanced solid tumours treated with RAD001 (everolimus), in which MAPK activation depended on the dosing schedule, plus a mouse prostate cancer model, xenografts and cell lines. The rise in MAPK is a response to mTORC1 inhibition; no study here measures what active mTORC1 does to ERK at steady state.
data.note: CAR2008 was already in the corpus but carried no edge until 2026-07-29.
